brief:
The International Criminal Court's arrest warrant for Benjamin Netanyahu remains valid regardless of his political standing, legal experts say, though his departure from office could alter enforcement dynamics. Netanyahu faces ICC prosecution over alleged war crimes in Gaza, but immunity as sitting prime minister does not extend to the court's jurisdiction. If Netanyahu loses Israel's upcoming election, he would lack the protections his office currently provides within Israel's legal system.

The warrant's continued validity after leaving office depends partly on whether other countries enforce ICC decisions and whether Netanyahu faces domestic prosecution, Middle East Eye reported. Israel is not an ICC member state and has rejected the court's authority. Netanyahu's political future remains uncertain following the election results.
dek: What happens to Netanyahu’s ICC warrant if he leaves office? Israel’s election has left Benjamin Netanyahu’s political future uncertain.
title: Netanyahu's ICC warrant status unclear if he loses office
